From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24,000,000; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law
**Status of Seller material:** Untrusted counterparty draft – reviewed critically. Note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter repeatedly *undercuts* the Seller Update (e.g. Bluefen consent "addressed" vs "NOT included"; Riverlark "addressed" vs "NOT repaid"). Those contradictions are leverage.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 100% of price for Fundamental/Title/Tax/IP; general cap no lower than ~30–50% given the thin disclosure, unresolved consents and known open issues; plus specific indemnities sitting *outside* the cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50% (floor 35%), with Fundamental, Tax, IP and all specific indemnities uncapped or at 100%. **Reason:** 20% is at the low end of the Australian mid-market range and is unjustified where the Seller's own letter leaves four material items (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006) unresolved.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis ~AUD 10,000–15,000 (with related/series claims aggregated); basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%); **tipping (first-dollar) basket**; no thresholds for Fundamental/Title/Tax or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter AUD 12,500 de minimis / AUD 150,000 tipping basket, with aggregation of related claims and carve-outs for Fundamental, Tax, IP and indemnities. **Reason:** An excess-only basket at ~1% plus a high de minimis means the Buyer absorbs the first AUD 250k of loss plus every sub-AUD 25k item – and the Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k) show how the Seller will try to fragment claims under the de minimis.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months; proposes all limitations apply to *all* Claims unless expressly stated otherwise (cl 12.3/13).
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months general (minimum one full audit cycle post-Completion); 7 years Tax; 6–7 years (or statute of limitations) for Fundamental/Title; IP/data at least 3 years; notification by reference to claim notice with a reasonable period (e.g. 9–12 months) to commence proceedings.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" default; insist on 24 months general and separate longer periods by category. **Reason:** 18 months may expire before the first full post-Completion audit, and the "all Claims" default sweeps indemnities and Fundamental Warranties into the shortest period by stealth.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental Warranties (title, capacity, authority, solvency, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, limitation period of 6–7 years or the statutory limit, no de minimis/basket, not subject to disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright.** **Reason:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that the Buyer could pay AUD 24m for shares and recover only AUD 4.8m if title fails – this is a market-standard carve-out and the Seller's proposal is a red flag on title (see SPA-N-015).

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply "to all Claims of any nature". No fraud carve-out appears anywhere in the Update or Disclosure Letter.
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out from every limitation (cap, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance, disclosure) for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller, the Company or their officers/advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a comprehensive fraud/wilful concealment carve-out as a non-negotiable. **Reason:** Purporting to limit liability for fraud is likely unenforceable in any event (and the non-reliance clause cannot exclude ACL s 18 misleading conduct claims), but the absence of the carve-out signals the Seller is trying to narrow remedies at the margins and must be fixed expressly.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (Sched 7; DL 1.1–1.2); cl 1.4 denies any admission of materiality or required action.
- **Buyer wants:** Disclosure only of matters *fairly disclosed* with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; data room disclosed only via a fixed, indexed USB/schedule attached to the Disclosure Letter; no disclosure against Fundamental Warranties; **no** disclosure by reference to public registers/searches.
- **Recommendation:** Accept data-room disclosure only with a "fair disclosure" standard and an agreed index; delete public-records disclosure; make the Disclosure Letter cut-off 22 September 2026 and require a bring-down at Completion. **Reason:** General disclosure of an unindexed data room plus public registers would effectively hollow out the warranty package, and the Seller's own letter admits the key DD items are incomplete.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter of which the Buyer *or its advisers* had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** No knowledge qualifier at all; if one must be given, limited to **actual** knowledge of a named short list of deal-team individuals, derived only from matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter – never constructive/imputed/adviser knowledge or "discoverable" matters.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3; fallback is actual knowledge of 2–3 named individuals only. **Reason:** "Discoverable from … public records" and adviser knowledge would convert every DD gap into a Buyer-side risk and effectively make the warranties worthless as a pricing/risk allocation tool.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Update says consent "is addressed"; Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the condition as satisfied on delivery of *any* written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter [2] admits no final written consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied. Bluefen = ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% FY26 revenue.
- **Buyer wants:** Bluefen consent as a **Condition Precedent** in Buyer-approved form, unconditional (or with cl 11.3 conditions satisfied and evidenced), from an authorised Bluefen signatory; Seller to use best endeavours; Buyer right to terminate and, ideally, a price adjustment/retention if consent is not obtained or is obtained on adverse terms.
- **Recommendation:** Hard CP in agreed form, Buyer waiver only, with an MAC-style termination right. **Reason:** 30% of revenue hangs on this consent and the Seller's "treat as satisfied on delivery of written consent" language would let a conditional or defective consent satisfy the CP.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL [3] confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Repayment and full discharge of security (deeds of release, PPSR discharges, ASIC Form 312/registered releases) **at Completion** as a deliverable, funded out of the purchase price via the funds flow, with payoff letter from Riverlark Bank pre-Completion; deduction of all Debt (incl. break costs and accrued interest) in the cash-free/debt-free adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; make payoff letter and executed releases Completion deliverables with direct payment to Riverlark from the price. **Reason:** A debt-free deal in which the Buyer acquires a company still subject to AUD 3.2m secured debt and a bank change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) is not debt-free, and the bank could call the facility at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow (DD-005). DL [5] confirms not in funds flow; silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus all on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, PAYG, leave accruals) treated as **Transaction Expenses/Debt** and deducted from the price or paid by the Seller through the funds flow; specific indemnity for any amount not so deducted; confirmation of conditions (continued-employment clawbacks) and that no further "change of control" entitlements exist.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct AUD 420k grossed up for on-costs (budget ~AUD 500k) from the price in the funds flow, backed by a specific indemnity. **Reason:** If the Company pays these post-Completion, the Buyer funds the Seller's transaction bonus – a direct leakage of ~2% of price.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000); "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4]: title to SOW3 Project Materials only passes on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment, and an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay covering all SOW1–3 deliverables (and moral rights consents); failing that, a retention/escrow and a broad indemnity covering loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, re-development costs and business interruption – uncapped or capped at 100% of price, not AUD 180k.
- **Recommendation:** Make the confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable and expand the indemnity to all loss arising from any defect in title to Ironquay-developed IP. **Reason:** The exposure is not the AUD 180k fee but ownership of the product's IP – for an analytics business that is the asset being bought.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 is "preliminary", "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sched 6); DL [6] admits scope (~1,240 records), access and notification obligations are all unknown and the investigation is incomplete.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of the investigation (with report delivered to Buyer) before Completion; Seller to meet any OAIC Notifiable Data Breach assessment/notification obligations pre-Completion; specific indemnity for all loss, regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation arising from the incident – outside cap, basket and time limits (minimum 3–6 years); warranty of no other incidents; possible retention.
- **Recommendation:** Specific uncapped indemnity plus investigation report as a CP/deliverable. **Reason:** A "preliminary" characterisation does not change the fact that an eligible data breach triggers statutory assessment timelines (30 days) and potential penalties that could exceed the entire general cap.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs" (DD-008/DD-011). DL [8] does not confirm whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation of whether the renewals are committed, their term and termination rights; if committed pre-Completion for post-Completion benefit, treat as accrued liabilities/working capital in the completion accounts; a warranty that no other material commitments outside the ordinary course exist; and – critically – treat the three as a **single related matter** for de minimis/basket purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Require full contract disclosure, pull into working capital/Debt as appropriate and add an aggregation clause for related claims. **Reason:** Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k pieces is exactly the pattern a high de minimis is designed to exploit.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All limitations, caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply uniformly to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5); Fundamental, Tax and IP folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes: (i) General Warranties – cap/basket/18–24m; (ii) Fundamental/Title – 100%/6–7y/no thresholds/no disclosure; (iii) Tax – 100%/7y/separate tax indemnity; (iv) IP & Data – higher cap/longer period; (v) Specific Indemnities (Riverlark, Bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Leakage) – outside all limitations; (vi) Fraud – no limitation.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft cl 12–13 as a matrix with express carve-outs; reject the "all Claims" default. **Reason:** A single-tier regime lets the lowest cap and shortest time limit govern the highest-risk exposures, which is the opposite of market allocation.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced solely by the Company's own share register at DD-012; DL [10] expressly notes this is "the source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification pre-signing: current ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller (share security), constitution and any shareholders' agreement/option/convertible instruments, chain of transfers and stamped transfer forms; Seller Fundamental Warranties on title, no encumbrances, no options/pre-emption rights; Completion deliverables of share transfer, share certificates (or indemnity for lost), updated register and ASIC Form 484.
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and make clean title a Fundamental Warranty with 100% cap. **Reason:** A self-maintained register is not evidence of title against third parties, and the Seller's attempt (SPA-N-004) to cap title warranties at 20% makes independent verification essential.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" – i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, AUD 250k basket, data-room disclosure.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate **Tax Indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, 100% cap, 7 years, no basket, pounds-for-pounds, covering income tax, GST, payroll tax, FBT, super guarantee, R&D tax incentive clawbacks given this is an analytics business); IP warranties covering ownership, registrations, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments (ties to Ironquay), no infringement, with a higher cap and 3+ year period; data/privacy warranties aligned to DD-006.
- **Recommendation:** Treat Tax and IP as **unsettled** and table a full Buyer tax deed and IP/data warranty schedule. **Reason:** The Seller's own letter shows IP title (Ironquay) and privacy (DD-006) are live, unresolved issues – they cannot be "settled" by a general regime that would time-bar them before the ATO's or OAIC's review windows even open.

---

## Summary of priority asks (for the mark-up cover note)

| Priority | Item | Headline ask |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SPA-N-008 Bluefen | Hard CP, agreed-form consent, cl 11.3 conditions evidenced |
| 1 | SPA-N-009 Riverlark | Payoff + releases at Completion, funded from price |
| 1 | SPA-N-004/014/015 Title & regime | Separate Fundamental regime, 100% cap, independent title checks |
| 1 | SPA-N-005 Fraud | Express fraud/wilful concealment carve-out |
| 2 | SPA-N-010 Bonuses | AUD 420k + on-costs deducted via funds flow + indemnity |
| 2 | SPA-N-011 Ironquay | Confirmatory IP assignment as deliverable; broad indemnity |
| 2 | SPA-N-012 DD-006 | Investigation report + uncapped specific indemnity |
| 2 | SPA-N-006/007 Disclosure & knowledge | Fair-disclosure standard; delete public-record disclosure & cl 8.3 |
| 3 | SPA-N-001/002/003 Caps, basket, time | 50% cap, AUD 12.5k/150k tipping, 24 months general |
| 3 | SPA-N-013/016 Sandbar, Tax/IP | Aggregation clause; full tax deed and IP/data schedule |

**Overall assessment:** The Seller Update describes items as "addressed", "adequate" or "settled" that the Seller's own Disclosure Letter admits are incomplete or unquantified. Recommend the Buyer's reply opens by listing those internal inconsistencies and framing the mark-up as bringing the SPA into line with the Seller's own disclosures.

Let me know if you want this converted into a clause-by-clause mark-up or an issues list in table form for the negotiation call.

- **Buyer wants:** Repayment and full discharge of security (deeds of release, PPSR discharges, ASIC Form 312/registered releases) **at Completion** as a deliverable, funded out of the purchase price via the funds flow, with payoff letter from Riverlark Bank pre-Completion; deduction of all Debt (incl. break costs and accrued interest) in the cash-free/debt-free adjustment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; make payoff letter and executed releases Completion deliverables with direct payment to Riverlark from the price. **Reason:** A debt-free deal in which the Buyer acquires a company still subject to AUD 3.2m secured debt and a bank change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) is not debt-free, and the bank could call the facility at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow (DD-005). DL [5] confirms not in funds flow; silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Bonuses plus all on-costs (superannuation, payroll tax, PAYG, leave accruals) treated as **Transaction Expenses/Debt** and deducted from the price or paid by the Seller through the funds flow; specific indemnity for any amount not so deducted; confirmation of conditions (continued-employment clawbacks) and that no further "change of control" entitlements exist.
- **Recommendation:** Deduct AUD 420k grossed up for on-costs (budget ~AUD 500k) from the price in the funds flow, backed by a specific indemnity. **Reason:** If the Company pays these post-Completion, the Buyer funds the Seller's transaction bonus – a direct leakage of ~2% of price.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000); "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL [4]: title to SOW3 Project Materials only passes on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion deliverables: evidence of cleared payment, and an executed **confirmatory IP assignment** from Ironquay covering all SOW1–3 deliverables (and moral rights consents); failing that, a retention/escrow and a broad indemnity covering loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, re-development costs and business interruption – uncapped or capped at 100% of price, not AUD 180k.
- **Recommendation:** Make the confirmatory assignment a Completion deliverable and expand the indemnity to all loss arising from any defect in title to Ironquay-developed IP. **Reason:** The exposure is not the AUD 180k fee but ownership of the product's IP – for an analytics business that is the asset being bought.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** DD-006 is "preliminary", "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sched 6); DL [6] admits scope (~1,240 records), access and notification obligations are all unknown and the investigation is incomplete.
- **Buyer wants:** Completion of the investigation (with report delivered to Buyer) before Completion; Seller to meet any OAIC Notifiable Data Breach assessment/notification obligations pre-Completion; specific indemnity for all loss, regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims and remediation arising from the incident – outside cap, basket and time limits (minimum 3–6 years); warranty of no other incidents; possible retention.
- **Recommendation:** Specific uncapped indemnity plus investigation report as a CP/deliverable. **Reason:** A "preliminary" characterisation does not change the fact that an eligible data breach triggers statutory assessment timelines (30 days) and potential penalties that could exceed the entire general cap.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are "ordinary-course operating costs" (DD-008/DD-011). DL [8] does not confirm whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Confirmation of whether the renewals are committed, their term and termination rights; if committed pre-Completion for post-Completion benefit, treat as accrued liabilities/working capital in the completion accounts; a warranty that no other material commitments outside the ordinary course exist; and – critically – treat the three as a **single related matter** for de minimis/basket purposes.
- **Recommendation:** Require full contract disclosure, pull into working capital/Debt as appropriate and add an aggregation clause for related claims. **Reason:** Splitting one AUD 330k commitment into three AUD 110k pieces is exactly the pattern a high de minimis is designed to exploit.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** All limitations, caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply uniformly to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5); Fundamental, Tax and IP folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Distinct regimes: (i) General Warranties – cap/basket/18–24m; (ii) Fundamental/Title – 100%/6–7y/no thresholds/no disclosure; (iii) Tax – 100%/7y/separate tax indemnity; (iv) IP & Data – higher cap/longer period; (v) Specific Indemnities (Riverlark, Bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Leakage) – outside all limitations; (vi) Fraud – no limitation.
- **Recommendation:** Redraft cl 12–13 as a matrix with express carve-outs; reject the "all Claims" default. **Reason:** A single-tier regime lets the lowest cap and shortest time limit govern the highest-risk exposures, which is the opposite of market allocation.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced solely by the Company's own share register at DD-012; DL [10] expressly notes this is "the source relied on" and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent verification pre-signing: current ASIC company extract and historical extract, PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller (share security), constitution and any shareholders' agreement/option/convertible instruments, chain of transfers and stamped transfer forms; Seller Fundamental Warranties on title, no encumbrances, no options/pre-emption rights; Completion deliverables of share transfer, share certificates (or indemnity for lost), updated register and ASIC Form 484.
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR searches now and make clean title a Fundamental Warranty with 100% cap. **Reason:** A self-maintained register is not evidence of title against third parties, and the Seller's attempt (SPA-N-004) to cap title warranties at 20% makes independent verification essential.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" – i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, AUD 250k basket, data-room disclosure.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate **Tax Indemnity** (pre-Completion tax, 100% cap, 7 years, no basket, pounds-for-pounds, covering income tax, GST, payroll tax, FBT, super guarantee, R&D tax incentive clawbacks given this is an analytics business); IP warranties covering ownership, registrations, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments (ties to Ironquay), no infringement, with a higher cap and 3+ year period; data/privacy warranties aligned to DD-006.
- **Recommendation:** Treat Tax and IP as **unsettled** and table a full Buyer tax deed and IP/data warranty schedule. **Reason:** The Seller's own letter shows IP title (Ironquay) and privacy (DD-006) are live, unresolved issues – they cannot be "settled" by a general regime that would time-bar them before the ATO's or OAIC's review windows even open.
